transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. Well, I came in because... I just feel completely flat inside. Even when my children come over to sit with me, or the sun is shining on my garden, I don't feel anything good. It's like the part of me that could be glad, or even just comforted, just... shut off.
Have you ever had periods in your life where you felt unusually energetic, talkative, or euphoric, lasting for several days at a time?
No, I haven't. I've never had anything like that happen. I've always been a pretty steady person, really, so I've never felt unusually energetic or euphoric for days on end like you're saying.
How long have you been feeling this way?
It's been about two weeks now. Ever since... well, since my husband collapsed. The paramedics were working on him right there in our kitchen. I've just felt this way ever since that happened.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or your ability to get a good night's sleep since this all started?
No, I haven't really noticed any changes there. My appetite is about the same as it always is, and I'm sleeping just fine. I just... I just feel so empty all the time.
Has this feeling of emptiness made it difficult for you to carry out your usual daily activities, like chores or taking care of yourself?

Yes, it really has. I... I've stopped going to the senior center completely. And I just can't seem to manage the meals or run my errands anymore. Even keeping track of my calendar is too much right now. My daughter has had to step in and do all of that for me. I mostly just stay in the house now, and... I avoid going into the kitchen entirely unless someone is in there with me.
Do you find yourself feeling unusually restless, worried, or on edge since that day?

Yes, I really do. When I’m in the house, I... I just keep listening for every little sound. I find myself constantly checking the hallway and making sure the back door is secure. And like I mentioned, I just don’t feel safe being in the kitchen by myself anymore. I'm just always on edge now.
Do you find yourself having unwanted, vivid memories or nightmares about the moment your husband collapsed?

No, I haven't really had anything like that. I mean, I remember it happening, of course, but I don't have those... vivid flashbacks or nightmares about it. I just try not to think about it when I don't have to.
Do you feel that the intensity of your distress or your inability to function is significantly greater than what one might expect given the circumstances of your husband's collapse?

I'm not really sure how to answer that. I mean... it was a terrible shock, seeing him collapse like that. I don't know what's considered normal or expected after something like this happens. 

I don't know if my reaction is worse than what other people would feel. I just know that I can't manage my life right now, and I can't even go into my own kitchen. I'm not sure what's expected, I just know it's too much for me to handle.

Are you finding that your feelings of being on edge and worried are focused specifically on the events surrounding your husband's health, or do you find yourself feeling this way about many different aspects of your daily life?

I'm... I'm not really sure how to answer that. I haven't really stopped to notice if it's just about his health or... or if it's everything else in my day. I just know I feel this way all the time right now. It's hard to separate it out. I'm just always worried, and I don't really know exactly what it's focused on at any given moment.
